section_summary: This section follows U.S. decisions about military yen, exchange rates, and Japanese currency during the occupation, including consultations with British, Chinese, and Soviet representatives. It also contains inquiries about Japanese currency held by individuals, Japanese banks and overseas assets, and the Soviet request to use 59 million yen in Japan. The final pages contain occupation directives on supplying yen to Allied representatives, taxation of aliens, and restitution of looted property.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: exchange rate for yen in outlying islands
subfiles.from: State Department, Financial and Monetary Affairs
subfiles.about: Points to Reinstein’s memorandum on exchange rates for military yen in Japanese outlying islands.
subfiles.summary: References a January 4 memorandum filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Pacific military exchange rates
subfiles.about: Points to Treasury comments on military exchange rates in Pacific areas.
subfiles.summary: References a January 9 Treasury paper filed elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Japanese currency and banks in the Philippines
subfiles.about: Requests information for China’s Finance Ministry on Japanese notes and banks after reoccupation of the Philippines.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether Japanese notes circulated and how Japanese banks were liquidated.

subfiles.title: Request for report from Manila
subfiles.about: Seeks a brief report to answer the Chongqing inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Requests facts on Japanese notes and bank liquidation in the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Interim reply to Chongqing
subfiles.about: Advises that Manila has been asked for the missing information.
subfiles.summary: Promises a further reply after Manila reports.

subfiles.title: Reply on Japanese notes and banks in the Philippines
subfiles.about: Reports that Japanese currency was outlawed and Japanese bank liquidation had not begun.
subfiles.summary: Japanese notes never circulated after reoccupation; bank assets were held by the Alien Property Custodian.

subfiles.title: Manila report on Japanese currency and banks
subfiles.about: Supplies the facts used in the Department’s reply to Chongqing.
subfiles.summary: Executive Order 25 outlawed Japanese currency; destroyed records delayed bank liquidation.

subfiles.title: Routing note on Rio despatch
subfiles.about: Routes a Rio de Janeiro despatch concerning a yen reimbursement claim.
subfiles.summary: Fragmentary routing note for the following claim.

subfiles.title: Brazilian yen reimbursement claim
subfiles.from: Duwayne G. Clark, U.S. Embassy, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Forwards Esther de Proença Lago’s claim for yen exchanged during diplomatic repatriation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses her letter seeking reimbursement for yen surrendered by her husband.

subfiles.title: Settlement of Lago reimbursement claim
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Rio de Janeiro
subfiles.about: Transmits a $138.90 check for 463 yen as final settlement.
subfiles.summary: Directs delivery of the check to Madame Lago.

subfiles.title: Illegible filing or routing note
subfiles.about: The surviving OCR does not establish the note’s subject.
subfiles.summary: Text largely illegible.

subfiles.title: Additional printing of Type B military yen
subfiles.about: Considers a War Department request to print six more months of Type B military yen.
subfiles.summary: McGuire suggests agreement that existing stocks will not delay a later change to an Allied designation.

subfiles.title: Conference on military yen design
subfiles.about: Records interdepartmental agreement on designs for military currency in Japan and Formosa.
subfiles.summary: Treasury will prepare two designs; the issuing authority’s wording remains undecided.

subfiles.title: Bessie Mae Young’s currency claim
subfiles.about: Asks how to claim dollar exchange for a Japanese note.
subfiles.summary: Requests conversion instructions for a purported $50 Japanese bill.

subfiles.title: Referral of Young’s letter
subfiles.about: Forwards Young’s inquiry to the agency thought responsible.
subfiles.summary: Standard interagency referral form.

subfiles.title: Reply to Bessie Mae Young
subfiles.about: States that the Department cannot advise a conversion route for her Japanese note.
subfiles.summary: Identifies the bill as probably 50 yen and declines to recommend conversion.

subfiles.title: Legal analysis of Young’s note
subfiles.about: Explains why Japanese notes provide no basis for a redemption claim.
subfiles.summary: Notes limited military conversion facilities and Treasury concern about yen speculation.

subfiles.title: Financial directives for Korea and Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of State for Secretary of the Treasury
subfiles.about: Reports occupation planning for currency, banks, and financial administration in Korea and Japan.
subfiles.summary: The proposed program would use military yen alongside Japanese notes at 15 yen per dollar for accounting, restrict currency flows, and place certain banks under guard. It asks for views on separate Korean currency, Japanese assets, and whether occupation orders should operate through the Japanese government.

subfiles.title: Military yen plans communicated to China
subfiles.about: Provides information for the Chinese government on supplemental military yen in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes Type B note markings, denominations, interchangeability with local currency, and the 15 yen per dollar military accounting rate. The rate is not a general exchange rate.

subfiles.title: Draft military yen message to Moscow
subfiles.about: Proposes telling the Soviet government about Type B military yen and its accounting rate.
subfiles.summary: Draft closely parallels the Chongqing message, covering note features, parity with Japanese currency, and the limited purpose of the 15 yen rate.

subfiles.title: Delivery of military currency information to Soviet government
subfiles.about: Reports delivery of a letter on Japan’s military currency to Vyshinsky.
subfiles.summary: Confirms transmission of the Department’s currency information.

subfiles.title: British Treasury comments on military yen
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy and Taylor, London; Winant
subfiles.about: Transmits British Treasury views on occupation currency and exchange rates in Japan.
subfiles.summary: British officials favor using Japanese supplied notes if dependable, with military currency held in reserve. They caution that the accounting rate should reflect Japanese prices and avoid worsening inflation or Japan’s postwar trade position. The embassy requests U.S. views.

subfiles.title: Young’s second currency request
subfiles.about: Sends a Japanese fifty-centavo note for exchange into dollars.
subfiles.summary: Renews her conversion request and encloses the note.

subfiles.title: Return of Young’s note
subfiles.about: Returns the note and explains that the Department cannot exchange it.
subfiles.summary: Says its value, if any, appears nominal.

subfiles.title: British War Office comments on military currency
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy and Taylor, London; Winant
subfiles.about: Transmits British concerns about currency supplied to Allied forces and differing island exchange rates.
subfiles.summary: The War Office seeks equal access to occupation currency and clear note identification. It would accept Bank of Japan notes if all forces used them. The embassy asks for rates and safeguards against movement of yen between areas.

subfiles.title: Reply to British currency questions
subfiles.about: Explains U.S. use of Bank of Japan notes and the revised Okinawa accounting rate.
subfiles.summary: States that 15 yen per dollar applies where yen currencies remain in circulation.

subfiles.title: Navy correction on Type B currency
subfiles.from: Rear Admiral John L. McCrea, Navy Department
subfiles.to: Chief, Foreign Activity Correlation Liaison, Department of State
subfiles.about: Corrects an earlier explanation of Type B military yen’s identification mark.
subfiles.summary: Type B is used in the Ryukyus; Type A was authorized for Korea.

subfiles.title: Treasury draft reply to London
subfiles.about: Proposes the Department’s answer to British comments on military yen.
subfiles.summary: Draft covers Japanese notes and the 15 yen Okinawa rate.

subfiles.title: Yen held by repatriates leaving Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Explains why U.S. agencies will not convert repatriates’ yen into dollars.
subfiles.summary: Army officers cannot pay for yen received free from the Bank of Japan; Japanese bank dollars remain blocked.

subfiles.title: Japanese assets in Siam
subfiles.about: Records agreement with Britain to seek seizure of Japanese assets in Siam.
subfiles.summary: British and U.S. representatives would jointly approach the Siamese government.

subfiles.title: Document transfer sheet
subfiles.about: Administrative sheet recording a file transfer.
subfiles.summary: No substantive document text survives.

subfiles.title: Japanese custody accounts abroad
subfiles.about: Suggests investigating Japanese diplomatic custody funds beyond Europe.
subfiles.summary: Cites Panama and proposes questioning the Yokohama Specie Bank about funds left with local custodians.

subfiles.title: Request for SCAP inquiry on custody accounts
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a cable seeking more information about Japanese custody accounts.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Dr. Fahs’s proposed cable for War Department approval.

subfiles.title: Proposed cable on custody accounts
subfiles.about: Seeks Yokohama Specie Bank records on diplomatic custody accounts in Latin America.
subfiles.summary: Specifically asks about cash left with local custodians.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Bern on Swiss role in Venezuela
subfiles.about: Asks whether the Swiss chargé in Caracas misunderstood instructions about Japanese property.
subfiles.summary: Requests clarification with the Swiss foreign office if needed.

subfiles.title: Swiss proposed transfer of Japanese interests
subfiles.about: Reports Swiss willingness to transfer Japanese funds and proposed responsibility for Japanese interests in Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: The Swiss chargé seeks a protocol transferring both property and protection duties.

subfiles.title: Rejection of Swiss protection clause
subfiles.about: Rejects a protocol clause making the United States Japan’s protecting power.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese request or U.S. agreement supports that responsibility.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about yen trading in Shanghai
subfiles.about: Asks whether Shanghai banks trade yen used for profitable conversion in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Investigates reports involving aircraft crews.

subfiles.title: Shanghai yen trading inquiry: reply
subfiles.about: Reports no reliable evidence yet on Shanghai banks trading yen.
subfiles.summary: Further inquiries will continue.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Shanghai inquiry reply
subfiles.about: Reproduces the March 29 report about possible Shanghai yen trading.
subfiles.summary: No reliable information has been found.

subfiles.title: Acheson–Novikov discussion of Soviet yen
subfiles.about: Records a Soviet request to spend 59 million yen in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Acheson receives an aide-mémoire and sees no immediate obstacle, pending review.

subfiles.title: Durbrow routing note on Soviet request
subfiles.about: Requests arrangements to give favorable consideration to the Soviet yen proposal.
subfiles.summary: Eastern European Affairs sees no objection.

subfiles.title: Soviet aide-mémoire on 59 million yen
subfiles.doc_type: aide-mémoire with original-language pages and translation
subfiles.about: Requests that 59 million yen be credited in a Japanese bank for Soviet use in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The cash comprises yen redeemed in southern Sakhalin and the Kurils plus prewar holdings. The Soviet government asks Washington to direct SCAP to arrange prompt deposit and use inside Japan.

subfiles.title: Soviet follow-up note on yen
subfiles.about: Urges a decision on the April 3 request concerning 59 million yen.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the proposed Japanese bank deposit and asks for expedited notice.

subfiles.title: Original-language Soviet follow-up note
subfiles.about: Original-language version of the Soviet request to expedite the yen decision.
subfiles.summary: Corresponds to the translated note on page 57.

subfiles.title: Draft interim reply to Soviet Embassy
subfiles.about: Says the broader issue of yen held outside Japan remains under review.
subfiles.summary: Explains that agencies are considering a general policy and have sought information from SCAP.

subfiles.title: Durbrow report on delay in Soviet yen decision
subfiles.about: Explains policy and inflation concerns delaying the Soviet request.
subfiles.summary: Billions of yen circulate outside Japan, so the Army seeks a general reconversion policy before accepting Soviet holdings. Officials also report Soviet deposits already arriving in Japan. Durbrow gives Novikov an interim explanation.

subfiles.title: Second Acheson–Novikov discussion
subfiles.about: Records Soviet requests concerning 59 million yen and a possible U.S. credit.
subfiles.summary: Novikov presses for a yen decision, and Acheson promises an interim reply. They also discuss whether Export-Import Bank funds remain available for a possible billion-dollar Soviet credit.

subfiles.title: Novikov’s oral statement on Soviet yen
subfiles.about: Restates the request for immediate deposit of 59 million yen in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes that neither the April 3 nor April 24 request has received a reply.

subfiles.title: War Department views on vessels supplied to the USSR
subfiles.about: Addresses disposition of vessels and barges supplied to the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: War Department sees no need for their return but recommends Navy-like terms and restrictions.

subfiles.title: Goetz’s yen inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about exchanging yen acquired in Japan for dollars.
subfiles.summary: The postcard was forwarded to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Reply to Goetz on converting yen
subfiles.about: Explains the limited facilities for converting yen acquired during service in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Neither government must convert the currency. Merchant seamen and service members had limited opportunities to reconvert legitimately acquired yen before leaving the theater; no general facility exists.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of occupation directives to Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Files directives on yen supply, alien taxation, and restitution.
subfiles.summary: Transmits certified copies of directives 55, 56, and 57.

subfiles.title: SWNCC transmittal of SCAP directives
subfiles.from: A. D. Reid, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.about: Provides copies of three directives already sent to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Designates copies for the Far Eastern Commission and State Department files.

subfiles.title: Interim procedures for supplying yen to Allied representatives
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Authorizes controlled yen advances for Allied official occupation expenses in Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP may supply reasonable yen amounts to Allied missions, representatives, and occupation forces. It must prevent excess issues and report advances monthly.

subfiles.title: Japanese taxation of aliens
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs nondiscriminatory Japanese taxation of aliens and limits capital levies on United Nations nationals.
subfiles.summary: Capital levies affecting United Nations nationals require exemptions or referral to the Far Eastern Commission. Further policy on extraordinary wartime taxes remains under consideration.

subfiles.title: Restitution of looted property
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets procedures to restore property and vessels taken from Allied countries by Japan.
subfiles.summary: The directive covers machinery, precious metals, securities, currency, cultural objects, raw materials, and ships. It defines claimants, delivery, costs, reparations interactions, and limits on Japanese exports of property subject to restitution. Allied vessels are to be returned as conditions permit, with a December 31, 1946 deadline.
